Known science foundations of Autonomous Star-System Infrastructure.

Deep-space autonomy flies today: AutoNav guided Deep Space 1, and Mars rovers drive themselves daily. Constellation management coordinates thousands of Starlink satellites. Delay-tolerant networking (DTN) is standardized for interplanetary links. Coordinating mining, manufacturing, and habitats as one system remains conceptual.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Autonomous Star-System Infrastructure.

Light-delay makes centralized control impossible; coordination must be distributed. Heterogeneous systems need common protocols that do not yet exist. A coordination failure could strand assets across the solar system.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 2.87 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is Earth-Mars light delay vs coordination messages per day (est.) at 2.87 orders of magnitude (coordination messages per day (est.) larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
